channel.title: Writing · Yenjia Chen
channel.description: Notes on what I'm learning and curious to explore, making knowledge and ideas easier to understand.

item.title: After you press Play: how Windows games run on Linux
item.description: Follow a Windows game from its executable to the GPU, and discover how Wine, Direct3D, Vulkan, DXVK and Proton bring it to Linux.

item.title: Drawing a raven with circles
item.description: The raven on this site's homepage is drawn by a chain of rotating circles. Change the number of circles and see how complex numbers, the discrete Fourier transform and Parseval's theorem turn an outline into a sum of rotations.

item.title: Fretboard scales and interval ear training
item.description: See any of eight scales across the first 12 frets, switch between note names and scale degrees, and train your ear to recognise the intervals between two notes.

item.title: Anatomy of an Electric Guitar
item.description: Rotate, zoom, and explore a 3D electric guitar. Discover 32 components, from the headstock and bridge to the electronics inside.

item.title: Basic guitar chords
item.description: 32 guitar chords, from basic to advanced. Switch between chord diagrams, tablature and staff notation, then practise with a tuner, strum patterns, looping playback and transposition.

item.title: How this website is built: Hugo, GitHub Pages, and Cloudflare
item.description: An introduction to static websites, Hugo, Blowfish, GitHub Actions, and hosting—and how to bring them together with a coding agent.

item.title: Sequence models without attention: from state space models to Mamba
item.description: Starting from sequence models and the limits of Transformers, a walk through state space models, discretization, HiPPO, S4, and Mamba's selective mechanism and hardware-aware algorithm.

item.title: LLaVA-Med: a vision-language model for medicine
item.description: A look at LLaVA-Med: connecting medical images and language through a two-stage training approach.

item.title: Information Bottleneck: visual, interpretable explanations for classification models
item.description: An intuitive introduction to Information Bottleneck Attribution, which uses the Information Bottleneck to explain image classifiers more precisely than Grad-CAM.
